message.content:
{"passages":[{"reference":"20.6","text":"When Peter heard these things, he became thoughtful for a little while and said, “I do not think anyone can discuss the evil one without doing the will of the evil one himself. Consequently, knowing this very thing, I do not know what I shall do—whether I shall remain silent or speak. If I were to remain silent, I would incur ridicule among the multitude, because, though professing to proclaim truth, I am ignorant of the discourse concerning evil. But if I were to speak, I fear that perhaps God is not pleased for evil to be investigated, but only good. Nevertheless, for you too, in response to Saphonius’s argument, I will make my own views clearer.

“I too agree that not everything belonging to human beings should be attributed to God. For example, human beings, since they do not have transformable bodies, do not transform themselves, but have a nature that is altered over time by changes. God, however, is not like this, for by his innate spirit and through an ineffable power, the body becomes whatever kind he wishes. And this is more readily believable than even that the air, having received such a nature from him, is transformed into dew by the incorporeal mind that permeates it and, when condensed, becomes water; water, when solidified, becomes stones and earth; and stones, when struck together, kindle fire. To such an extent, through alteration and transformation, the air, after first becoming water, ended in fire through these transformations, and what was wet was changed into the opposite nature.

“What then? Did God not also transform Moses’s staff into a living creature, making it a snake, which he transformed back again into a staff? And through that very staff which had been transformed, he changed the water of the Nile into blood, which he also transformed back again into water. Moreover, by an inbreathing of breath he transformed the human being, who was dust, into flesh, and transformed him back again into dust. And was not Moses, though himself flesh, transformed into an exceedingly great light, so that the sons of Israel were unable to look directly at him? Much more, therefore, is God supremely able to transform himself into whatever he wishes.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"περὶ πονηροῦ διαλεγόμενον μὴ αὐτοῦ τοῦ πονηροῦ τὸ θέλημα ποιεῖν","chosen":"discuss the evil one without doing the will of the evil one himself","rationale":"The repeated substantival πονηρός is rendered personally as “the evil one.” The broader alternative “discuss evil without doing the will of evil itself” remains grammatically possible."},{"source_quote":"τὰ σώματα τρεπτὰ","chosen":"transformable bodies","rationale":"The adjective describes bodies as capable of being changed or transformed."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ταύτῃ μᾶλλον ἔστι πιστεῦσαι, ἢ καὶ ὁ ἀὴρ","chosen":"And this is more readily believable than even that the air","rationale":"The rendering preserves the comparison signaled by μᾶλλον ... ἢ rather than replacing ἢ with a causal conjunction. The resulting comparison is contextually difficult. A disjunctive reading, “or even the air,” is possible for ἢ καί, but μᾶλλον favors the comparative construction."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ αὐτὸν διήκοντος ἀσωμάτου νοῦ","chosen":"the incorporeal mind that permeates it","rationale":"The participle depicts the incorporeal mind as extending throughout the air."},{"source_quote":"εἰς μέγιστον ἐτράπη φῶς","chosen":"was transformed into an exceedingly great light","rationale":"The wording describes transformation into light, not merely an act of shining."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"λίθοι.δὲ","issue":"The confirmed print places a period between λίθοι and δὲ without a following space, although the words continue the coordinated description. The translation treats δὲ as continuing the sentence, but that interpretation of the printed punctuation remains provisional.","proposed_reading":"λίθοι δὲ","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.7","text":"“But perhaps one of you has considered that one thing can be made into something by another, whereas someone cannot transform himself into whatever he wishes, and that transformation belongs to what grows old and has ..... to die. But one must not think this about immortal beings. For were not angels, ageless ...... and of fiery substance, transformed into flesh, and those in Abraham’s presence who had been ...........ed, whose feet human beings even washed as the feet of humans of the same substance? Moreover, an angel wrestled with Jacob, who was a human being, after being transformed into flesh so that he could come into bodily contact with him. After wrestling evenly with him, when the angel wished, he was transformed back into his own nature. Then, changing into fire, he did not burn Jacob’s broad sinew, but scorched it and made him lame.

“Now whoever cannot become something else whenever he wishes is mortal, since he is subject to his own nature. But whoever is able to become whatever he wishes whenever he wishes, since he is master of nature itself and returns to youth, is immortal. Therefore, much more does the power of God transform the substance of the body into whatever it wishes whenever it wishes, and it brings forth something of the same substance, without a transformation being present, but not something equal in power. For the one who brings forth can also transform again into another substance what has been turned toward himself, whereas the one brought forth, being also a child of the transformation originating from that one, cannot become anything else without the will of the one who brought him forth, unless that one wishes it.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"συγχρωτισθῆναι","chosen":"come into bodily contact","rationale":"The rare verb denotes close physical contact; “grapple with him” is also possible in this wrestling context."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ὁμοούσιον μὴ παρούσῃ τροπῇ προβάλλει, ἰσοδύναμον δὲ οὔ","chosen":"and it brings forth something of the same substance, without a transformation being present, but not something equal in power","rationale":"μὴ παρούσῃ τροπῇ is read circumstantially as a dative-absolute construction: no transformation is present or taking place during the projection. An instrumental reading, “by a transformation that is not present,” is grammatically possible but contextually obscure. ὁμοούσιον and ἰσοδύναμον are treated as substantival adjectives."},{"source_quote":"ὁμοούσιον","chosen":"something of the same substance","rationale":"The compositional rendering preserves the claim of shared substance without importing a later doctrinal formulation."},{"source_quote":"ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν τραπέντα δύναται","chosen":"can also transform again into another substance what has been turned toward himself","rationale":"The act of transforming is supplied elliptically from the preceding discussion. Alternatively, ἐφ’ ἑαυτόν may concern action upon or under the authority of the one who brings forth; the compressed construction does not identify the relationship unambiguously."},{"source_quote":"ὁ δὲ προβληθεὶς τῆς ἐξ ἐκείνου τροπῆς τε καὶ τέκνον ὑπάρχων","chosen":"whereas the one brought forth, being also a child of the transformation originating from that one","rationale":"The genitive τῆς ... τροπῆς is retained as a relationship of origin rather than turning τροπή into a nominative predicate. Alternatively, it may indicate the projected being’s derivation—“being of the transformation from that one”—with καὶ τέκνον adding the further description “and being a child.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καὶ ἀποθανεῖν ..... ἔχοντος","issue":"The selected edition prints a five-dot lacuna between ἀποθανεῖν and ἔχοντος. Its content is unavailable; all five dots are retained and no restoration is supplied.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἄγγελοι ἀγήρως ...... καὶ πυρώδους οὐσίας","issue":"The selected edition prints a six-dot lacuna after ἀγήρως. All six dots remain explicit, and the unavailable wording has not been restored.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"οἱ παρὰ τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ........... σθέντες","issue":"The selected edition prints an eleven-dot lacuna before the surviving passive participial fragment σθέντες. The English “...........ed” represents the printed gap and recoverable passive morphology without conjecturing a lexical stem.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.8","text":"When Peter had said these things, Micaiah, who was himself one of the companions following him, said, “I too would like to learn from you whether, just as the evil one came into being, so also the good one came into being. If they came into being in the same way, they seem to me to be brothers.”

Peter replied, “They did not come into being in the same way, if indeed you remember what I said at the beginning: the fourfold substance of the evil one’s body, having been carefully differentiated by God, was brought forth; but when that substance had been mixed externally according to the will of the one who brought it forth, the disposition that delights in evils arose in connection with the mixture. Thus one should understand that the fourfold substance brought forth from God is God’s child and itself exists eternally, whereas the disposition that delights in evils arose afterward as an accidental feature of the substance mixed externally by him. Thus it was neither begotten by God nor by anyone else; neither was it brought forth by him, nor did it come forth spontaneously, nor did it always exist, as the substance did before the commingling. Rather, in accordance with God’s will, it occurred accidentally in the external mixing. We have said many times that this must be so.

“But the good one, having been begotten from God’s most beautiful transformation and not having occurred accidentally through an external mixing, is truly a son. Nevertheless, since these things are unwritten and have been made credible by conjectures, let the ....... not be confirmed as certainly being so. Otherwise, the mind, as though it had certainly grasped ...........es, ceases from searching. And remember those instructions of mine too: such things must not be told to .......n, but to those who have proved most trustworthy after testing. Nor should such things be asserted lightly even among yourselves, and you ought not dare to speak as though you had precisely established the discovery of secret things. Rather, you should remain silent and only ponder them. For in speaking, the one who utters them may perhaps sin as one who does not know, and will incur punishment for having dared—even to himself—to utter things honored by silence.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τετραγενὴς","chosen":"fourfold","rationale":"The adjective describes the substance as constituted in fourfold fashion; “four-element” is a possible cosmological interpretation."},{"source_quote":"πεφιλοκρινημένη","chosen":"having been carefully differentiated","rationale":"The verb denotes careful discrimination or separation. “Carefully selected” is possible, but the surrounding mixture terminology favors differentiation."},{"source_quote":"ἔξω δὲ αὐτῆς κατὰ τὴν τοῦ προβαλόντος βουλὴν κραθείσης πρὸς τὴν κρᾶσιν ἡ κακοῖς χαίρουσα προαίρεσις","chosen":"but when that substance had been mixed externally according to the will of the one who brought it forth, the disposition that delights in evils arose in connection with the mixture","rationale":"αὐτῆς is taken as the subject of the genitive absolute and as referring to the already mentioned fourfold substance; ἔξω describes its external mixing. Alternatively, ἔξω αὐτῆς may mean “outside it,” with an unexpressed subject of κραθείσης, but that reading would imply an additional constituent not explicitly named here."},{"source_quote":"ἡ συμβεβηκυῖα κακοῖς χαίρουσα προαίρεσις ἐπεγένετο","chosen":"the disposition that delights in evils arose afterward as an accidental feature","rationale":"The wording distinguishes the contingent disposition from the underlying substance and states that it arose subsequently."},{"source_quote":"στοχασμοῖς πεπιστωμένα","chosen":"made credible by conjectures","rationale":"The phrase refers to reasoned conjectures or inferences rather than certain demonstrations."},{"source_quote":"οὐχ ὡς ἔχων","chosen":"as one who does not know","rationale":"The phrase literally describes the speaker as not possessing something, with knowledge or secure understanding supplied from context. “As one who does not possess it” is a more formal alternative."},{"source_quote":"τὰ σιγῇ τετιμημένα","chosen":"things honored by silence","rationale":"The expression presents silence as the honor properly accorded to secret matters."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"μὴ πάντως ἡ ....... οὕτως ἔχειν βεβαιούσθω","issue":"The selected edition prints a seven-dot lacuna after the feminine article ἡ. The missing subject cannot be recovered from the supplied wording, so all seven dots are retained without restoration.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὁ νοῦς ὡς πάντως προειληφὼς ........... ες τοῦ ζητεῖν παύεται","issue":"The selected edition prints an eleven-dot lacuna followed by the surviving fragment ες. The translation retains the eleven dots and represents the fragment as “es”; no complete word is conjectured.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὅτι τὰ τοιαῦτα .......ν οὐ δεῖ λέγειν","issue":"The selected edition prints a seven-dot lacuna before the surviving final ν. The translation retains all seven dots and represents the surviving fragment as “n” without restoring the missing word.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.9","text":"When Peter had said these things, a certain Lazarus, himself one of the followers, said, “Tell us how the reconciliation is possible: how can it be reasonable for the evil one, who was appointed by a righteous God to be the punisher of those who acted impiously, later to be sent with his angels and the sinners into the lower darkness? For I remember that the Teacher himself said this too.”

Peter said, “I too acknowledge that the evil one does nothing evil in this respect, insofar as he carries out the law given to him. Although he has an evil disposition, nevertheless, because of his fear of God, he does nothing unjustly. But because he slanders teachers of truth as a snare for the undiscerning, this same being is also called the Slanderer.

“As for our truthful Teacher’s saying that he and his angels would depart with the deceived sinners into the lower darkness, it has an explanation like this. The evil one, having been allotted a constitution that delights in darkness, descends with his fellow-servant angels into the darkness of Tartarus and takes pleasure in it, for darkness is congenial to fire. But human souls, being drops of pure light, are drunk in together by a substance of alien fire; and since they do not have a nature capable of dying, they are punished according to their deserts.

“But if the ruler of wickedness, being a human being, is not sent into the darkness because he does not delight in it, then this constitution of his that delights in evils can be recombined into the good one’s disposition, and thus, as good, he will be judged to coexist. This is all the more so because, although he had been allotted a constitution that delights in evils, on account of his fear of God he did nothing contrary to what seemed right to God’s law. And surely, when the high priest Aaron’s staff became a snake and was transformed back again into a staff, Scripture mystically foreshadowed this with reference to the recombination of the evil one’s transformation, which will take place later and which is yet to be.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Τὴν συμφωνίαν ἡμῖν εἰπὲ","chosen":"Tell us how the reconciliation is possible","rationale":"συμφωνία denotes agreement or consistency; Lazarus asks how the apparently conflicting claims can be reconciled. “Tell us the consistency” is a more formal alternative."},{"source_quote":"διάβολος","chosen":"Slanderer","rationale":"This preserves the explicit association with the preceding act of slandering. The conventional title “Devil” is an alternative."},{"source_quote":"κρᾶσιν","chosen":"constitution","rationale":"The noun literally denotes a mixture but here refers to the being’s composite constitution."},{"source_quote":"συμπινόμεναι","chosen":"are drunk in together","rationale":"The passive participle preserves the drinking image applied to drops of pure light being taken into alien fire."},{"source_quote":"μετασυγκριθῆναι εἰς ἀγαθοῦ προαίρεσιν","chosen":"be recombined into the good one’s disposition","rationale":"The genitive ἀγαθοῦ is taken substantivally as “of the good one.” A qualitative reading, “into a disposition toward good,” is contextually possible but less directly reflects the genitive construction."},{"source_quote":"ἀγαθὸς συνεῖναι κριθήσεται","chosen":"as good, he will be judged to coexist","rationale":"ἀγαθός is taken predicatively of the ruler of wickedness. Alternatively, it may be substantival—“the good one will be judged to coexist”—though the companion with whom he coexists would remain implicit."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"γενησομένην τῆς τροπῆς μετασύγκρισιν μυστηριωδῶς ἡ γραφὴ ἐσομένην","issue":"Both γενησομένην and ἐσομένην appear to describe the feminine μετασύγκρισιν, producing a redundant and syntactically awkward pair of future expressions. The confirmed printed wording is represented by “which will take place later and which is yet to be” rather than emended.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.10","text":"After Lazarus, Joseph—himself also one of the followers—said, “Correctly, everything sa.....; and grant me this too, since I wish to learn: why, for everyone, from the same words ......... some are persuaded, while others refuse to believe?”

Peter said, “The words are not incantations, so that anyone who hears must necessarily believe. Rather, the fact that some are persuaded and others are not intelligently demonstrates freedom of choice.”

We all blessed him who had said these things.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐπῳδαί","chosen":"incantations","rationale":"The noun denotes charms or magical spells intended to compel an effect, contrasting with freely given belief."},{"source_quote":"πάντως","chosen":"necessarily","rationale":"The adverb expresses the inevitability that would characterize an incantation’s effect."},{"source_quote":"αὐτεξούσιον","chosen":"freedom of choice","rationale":"The term denotes self-determination or freedom of agency."},{"source_quote":"ἀπειθοῦσι","chosen":"refuse to believe","rationale":"The verb can express disbelief, resistance, or disobedience; the immediate contrast with being persuaded favors “refuse to believe.”"},{"source_quote":"ταῦτα εἰπόντα οἱ πάντες εὐλογήσαμεν","chosen":"We all blessed him who had said these things","rationale":"The accusative participle εἰπόντα describes the object of εὐλογήσαμεν. Peter is its contextual referent; the construction is not an unexpressed object followed by a temporal participle."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"Ὀρθῶς πάντα εἴρ.....","issue":"The selected edition prints a five-dot lacuna after the surviving beginning εἴρ. That beginning is recognizable as part of a saying-verb, but the unavailable ending could determine person, voice, and other grammatical information. The fragmentary English “sa.....” preserves the five dots without supplying those unavailable features.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"διὰ τί πᾶσι τῶν αὐτῶν λόγων ......... οἱ μὲν πείθονται","issue":"The selected edition prints a nine-dot lacuna between λόγων and οἱ. The surviving syntax remains incomplete; all nine dots are retained, and no missing verb or participle is restored.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
